text: You are going to investigate what happens to the temperature when two different solids, W and X,
dissolve in water.
Read all the instructions carefully before starting the experiments.
Instructions
You are going to carry out two experiments.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe the appearance of solution Y.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
Add a few drops of aqueous sodium hydroxide to the first portion of solution Y and shake
the test-tube to mix the solutions.
Record your observations.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Now add an excess of aqueous sodium hydroxide to the mixture.
Record your observations.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text:
Pour the mixture from (b)(ii) into a boiling tube and add a small piece of aluminium foil.
Heat the mixture carefully. Test the gas produced with indicator paper.
Record your observations.

Keep the second portion of solution Y for the test in (e).
tests on solution Z
Divide the solution into three equal portions in three test-tubes.

text: You are provided with two solutions, Y and Z.
Carry out the following tests on the solutions, recording all of your observations at each stage.
tests on solution Y
Divide the solution into two equal portions in two test-tubes.
Washing soda crystals are crystals of hydrated sodium carbonate, Na CO3.10H O. When exposed
to the air, some of the water is lost from the crystals and a new substance is formed. This process
occurs faster in hotter climates.
Plan an experiment to determine the percentage of water by mass present in the new substance.
